title: Run a Multi-File Change in Stages
subtitle: Advanced · Scoped implementation in GCP

sources.label: DORA on working in small batches

scenes.title: Set a narrow goal
scenes.body: The synthetic refactor shares a rule across two callers.
scenes.code:
Issue #31 · Centralize the order quantity rule
Accept positive integers. Reject 0 and negatives.
Preserve current CLI and API outputs.
Scope: shared rule and its two callers.
scenes.narration: The CLI and API in this synthetic order service both validate quantity, and the rule is duplicated. Issue thirty-one asks us to share the validator and keep the behavior of both callers. Open the issue and point to the expected outputs before asking for edits. We want a small structural change with the same results for the same inputs.
scenes.focus: Preserve the CLI and API behavior
scenes.action: Read issue 31 and mark the allowed files.

scenes.title: Record the behavior before editing
scenes.body: The baseline covers both callers and quantity boundaries.
scenes.code:
git status --short --branch
git rev-parse --short HEAD
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
scenes.narration: Run the existing suite first. The synthetic baseline shows eight passing tests, including normal and boundary cases around the two callers. Capture the starting commit and command with that result. This gives us a comparison point after each stage. If a boundary isn't already covered, agree on how to capture it before you ask the agent to move the rule.
scenes.focus: Eight tests pass before any edit
scenes.action: Check the branch and save the starting test run.

scenes.title: Ask for one stage at a time
scenes.body: Put a human checkpoint between the proposed edits.
scenes.code:
1. Extract the rule and migrate the CLI.
2. Migrate the API caller after I review stage 1.
Show the files and run the approved focused checks.
scenes.result: Approve only the shared rule and CLI stage.
scenes.narration: Ask the agent to map the two callers and propose one stage for each migration. The first stage extracts the rule and points the CLI at it. The second stage changes the API. Check that the agent can name the files and validation command. Then approve the first stage and leave the second stage waiting for the diff and test evidence.
scenes.focus: Stage 1 changes the CLI; stage 2 changes the API
scenes.action: Ask for the plan and confirm the first stage only.

scenes.title: Inspect the first implementation
scenes.body: Check the updated call without losing existing outputs.
scenes.code:
git status --short
git diff -- orders/quantity.py orders/cli.py
scenes.result:
Shared rule copied into is_valid_quantity.
CLI now calls is_valid_quantity(value).
scenes.narration: Look at Git status first so a newly created file is visible. In the example, the shared validator and the CLI are the only files changed. Open the validator and check the comparison, then follow the call in the CLI. The tests should still show the same behavior for quantity one, zero, and negative values. Review that evidence before the API stage.
scenes.focus: The shared validator and CLI are the only changes
scenes.action: Open the shared rule and CLI diff.

scenes.title: Pause a change outside the issue
scenes.body: The deployment file is unrelated to this synthetic issue.
scenes.code:
Proposed: orders/api.py       in scope
Proposed: infra/deploy.yaml   outside scope

Keep the edit limited to the API call site.
scenes.narration: Here's the staged handoff. The agent proposes opening the API and a deployment file. Pause on the deployment entry. The issue names an API caller and a behavior check, so there is no reason to approve that file in this step. Tell the agent which call site belongs to the scope and ask for a revised plan before it edits anything further.
scenes.focus: infra/deploy.yaml is outside the approved scope
scenes.action: Stop and ask for a narrower API proposal.

scenes.title: Recheck the whole change
scenes.body: Compare the current result with the starting evidence.
scenes.code:
git status --short
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
scenes.result:
orders/quantity.py · orders/cli.py · orders/api.py
Synthetic final result: 8 tests pass.
scenes.narration: After the API stage, confirm the names of all three changed files and inspect the new call. Run the same test command again, on the final state. Here all eight tests still pass. Compare the observed boundary cases with the baseline and check the public outputs. The final run is the one that supports this exact diff.
scenes.focus: Three expected files; the same eight tests pass
scenes.action: Review status, then rerun the baseline suite.

scenes.title: Turn the checkpoints into review evidence
scenes.body: Link the synthetic issue and capture compatibility checks.
scenes.code:
Issue #31 · shared validator and two callers
Baseline: 8 pass
Final: 8 pass
CLI and API outcomes checked
scenes.result: Independent reviewer verifies using GitHub CLI.
scenes.narration: The pull request can now explain what changed, what stayed compatible, and how we checked it. Include both runs and the scope decision about the deployment file. A separate human reviewer can inspect the diff and check status using GitHub CLI from the authorized terminal. They can follow the same evidence trail without having to watch your agent session.
scenes.focus: The reviewer can connect both test runs to the diff
scenes.action: Prepare the PR summary with the stage evidence.

scenes.title: Repeat the pattern on another small refactor
scenes.body: Choose your stop and approval points before editing.
scenes.code:
Baseline → plan → first caller → verify
                     second caller → verify → PR
scenes.narration: For practice, find a second repeated rule in the training checkout. Decide what the first stage proves and what the second stage proves. Keep both stages small enough to explain in a sentence. If you can point to a baseline, a stop point, and a final independent check, you have a refactoring workflow you can reuse.
scenes.focus: Each stage has one testable outcome
scenes.action: Repeat the pattern with two small callers.
